get.description:
EPC tracking allows you to gather valuable click data. You will see estimated revenues for single clicks after round about 2h depending on our system load. After we receive final Revenue data from our Partner we’ll apply corrections to the estimated revenue, so the data will match with our system-wide statistical data. *

Experimental feature
We introduced cursor-based pagination for experimental reasons. As a result, please be aware of the following potential changes depending on system conditions:
  • Under large system load, we may reduce capacity
  • We may introduce new rate limits
  • We may rethink the entire architecture of cursor based endpoint(s)

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The date of the day you want to receive (PST/PDT)

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: On your first request, the server runs the query and generates a result set. To retrieve the next page, pass the `nextToken` value from the `cursor` object in the previous response. Without a token, the first page is always returned. Result sets expire automatically — the exact time is shown in `expiresAt` and is determined by the server based on the requested data; it cannot be influenced by the caller.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Results per page. You can set upto 999 results per page

get.description:
This report contains tracking data and non final numbers. Most publishers use this to monitor, analyze and optimize the click through rate from view of the keywords page to ad click.
Without a 'columns' parameter every row carries the full default set (session/campaign/device/country/etc., the standard tracking-link parameters and the revenue figures). Tracking-link parameters are always grouped under a nested 'querystring' object.

Revenue columns. pre_estimation, estimation and estimation_5h are three estimates of the same revenue. Each one is more accurate than the one before it and each one becomes available later: pre_estimation is the earliest and roughest figure, estimation follows about 40 minutes after the click, and estimation_5h is the most accurate of the three and settles about five hours after the click. None of them is final - a row keeps improving over the course of the day, so fetching the same day again later returns better numbers.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The single day you want to receive the session report for (PST/PDT). Must not be in the future or more than 50 days in the past.

parameters.name: campaignType
parameters.description:
Type of campaigns to report. Default 'rsoc'
Available Values : rsoc

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description:
Which columns to return, in the order you want them. Omit the parameter to get the full default set; if you do specify it, name at least one column.

Any column of the report:.
campaign_id, campaign_type, campaign_name, date, timestamp, clicks, keyword, device_type, country, user_agent, session, browser_language, pre_estimation, estimation, estimation_5h.

A tracking-link parameter as querystring.<parameter> - one of the standard ones (querystring.subid1 to querystring.subid4, querystring.network, querystring.site, querystring.siteid, querystring.adtitle) or any custom one your tracking link uses, e.g. querystring.myCustomParam.

querystring for the entire raw querystring, returned as querystring_raw.

Requested tracking-link parameters always end up inside the nested querystring object, positioned where the first of them was requested.
Pass multiple values separated by commas.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Column to sort the report by: any of the fixed columns listed above. Default 'timestamp'.

parameters.name: orderOrientation
parameters.description:
The result order direction:
asc - Ascending; from A to Z
desc - Descending; from Z to A. Default 'desc'.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Results per page. You can set up to 1000 results per page. Default 1000.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Result offset

patch.description:
You can change campaign names, status, imprint settings, keyword amount, keywords, S2S callbacks, or tracking targets.
Endpoint requires an array of datasets in post body.

The entire request fails if:

  • Only `id` is provided for any dataset
  • Any validation error occurs
  • More than 100 datasets are sent
  • Any campaign update fails

Status
Activating a campaign that is not ready will set it to `pending` until all requirements are met.

S2S Callbacks
A GET request is sent to the provided URL, with placeholders replaced by matching query parameters.

Placeholders:
`{campaign_id}`, `{campaign_name}`, `{currency}`, `{device}`, `{event_id}`, `{keyword}`, `{revenue}`, `{timestamp}`, `{type}`


All tracking link URL parameters can be used as placeholders. If you include a parameter named foo=bar in the tracking link, the template variable {foo} will be available and replaced with bar.


Example: https://tracktest.com/?subid1=test1&subid2=test2&source=network&type={type}&foo={foo}


Notes:

  • URLs must start with http:// or https://
  • Callbacks are campaign-specific
  • If 100+ errors occur without a successful call, callbacks are paused
  • Global S2S settings are used by default; campaign-level settings override them

id.description: Campaign ID to update. Must be provided for each dataset.

imprint.description: Enable or disable imprint for this campaign

keywords.description: List of keywords for this campaign

s2sCallbacks.description: Object with callback URLs for each event type

viewRt.description: URL for viewRt (realted term click) callback

estimatedRevenue5h.description: URL for estimated revenue after 5 hours callback

skipStatusCheck.description: If true, skips the live HTTP status check for the S2S callback URLs in this dataset. Useful for URLs containing placeholders (e.g. click_id) that only resolve to a real value at runtime.

columns.description:
List of columns like 'campaign_name' and 'device_type'.
  • You can also specify all parameters of your tracking-link you sent to tonic (e.g. siteid, subid1, subid4, adtitle).
  • If you add 'querystring', the whole querystring comes up in a separate column.
  • For RSoC Campaigns: If you add 'problematic_ad_id', preferably in addition to 'ad_id', you will receive a column that identifies with yes/no whether the received 'ad_id' looks suspicious.
  • For RSoC Campaigns: The columns 'ad_blocked' and 'ad_blocked_reason' are available, specifying whether a redirect was not monetized and why.
  • For RSoC Campaigns: The column 'rsoc_unit_loaded' indicates whether our feed provider decided to deliver the RSoC unit (true/false). If empty, this information was not received.

schedule.description: The schedule of the report. Default: 'on-demand'.

phrases.description:
Phrases to guide content generation. Ensure these align with the article and preceding ad creatives. For example, if the ad promotes 'weight loss', the article should provide comprehensive weight loss advice, not general health tips or unrelated topics.
  • Create 3-5 phrases that expand on the teaser, maintaining consistency and relevance throughout the article.
  • Use these phrases to create detailed and informative sections that support the main topic. Ensure all content is original and not misleading.
  • Avoid content that overpromises or misleads the reader.

Either 'phrases' or 'title' or both must be provided. If phrases are provided, the title becomes optional.

title.description:
A concise and accurate title that clearly represents the content of the article and aligns with the initial ad creatives. Avoid misleading or exaggerated claims.
  • Ensure the title is specific and relevant to the article's topic. Do not use sensational language or promises that can't be delivered.
  • Avoid using phrases that imply a reward or incentive for clicking. Do not include concrete prices, false endorsements, or time-sensitive offers.

Either 'title' or 'phrases' or both must be provided. If phrases are not provided, this field becomes required.
Required when 'phrases' is empty or not provided

teaser.description:
An engaging opening paragraph that gives a clear idea of the article's content. Avoid vague or overly broad statements.
  • The teaser should provide enough information to capture interest without making false promises. Ensure it aligns with the headline and main content.
  • Avoid references to sensitive issues or promises of unrealistic outcomes.
  • The teaser should be at least 250 characters long, with a maximum length of 1000 characters.

citationLink.description: You may add 1 URL from a reputable third-party source that provides factual validation for the article's content. This enhances the credibility of your ad flow while ensuring compliance. Please note, this feature is not available by default and needs to be enabled for your account. Contact your account manager for more information.
